facts.text: Bela Vista, also called Bixiga, is São Paulo's historic “Little Italy” where Italian immigrants settled in late 19th century.
The neighborhood’s name comes from Chácara do Bexiga, a farm owned by Antônio José Leite Braga nicknamed “Bexiga” for smallpox scars.
Bela Vista hosts the oldest samba school in São Paulo, Vai-Vai, founded in the early 20th century.
The parish of Nossa Senhora da Achiropita, established to serve immigrants, hosts an annual Achiropita procession and August street food fair.
Teatro Oficina, with its experimental architecture, and Teatro Brasileiro de Comédia, founded in 1948, shaped modern Brazilian drama in Bela Vista.
The area’s hilly terrain shaped its street layout, giving Bela Vista distinctive vistas amid dense urban development.
